key_insight: A foundation-model-based, data-efficient pipeline can detect duodenal epithelial neoplasia from whole-slide histology with strong performance despite very limited rare-tumour training data.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help pathologists triage duodenal biopsy slides more consistently across hospitals, especially for rare lesions where labelled examples are scarce.
method: 10x H&E whole-slide biopsy patches were encoded with the Hibou-B foundation model.
Patch embeddings were reduced with PCA, clustered by a Gaussian mixture model, and classified with a Random Forest.
Performance was compared using global versus site-specific standardisation and tested with leave-one-hospital-out validation plus an external hospital cohort.
evidence_signal: Across 8,027 normal and 401 neoplastic biopsies from five hospitals, the model reached 90% mean cross-validation accuracy and 94% accuracy on an independent external test hospital.
watch_item: The dataset is still relatively small for rare neoplasms and performance may vary with slide preparation, scanner differences, or deployment to new sites.
paper_title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
